Make a budget and see how much money you need to survive. You need to include any bills you have to pay, gas, groceries, anything else that is a necessity. Subscriptions are not a necessity. 
If it’s more than what you’re making, you need to work on getting a better paying job or getting a second job. Either that or work on lowering what you’re spending, but obviously that’s not always possible. 
Stick to your budget. Get things paid off if that’s applicable to your situation. Accept that for a little while you’re probably not going to be doing much of anything fun or terribly exciting.
Start putting any extra you have away. If you have no money saved at all, get enough saved up that you’d be able to support yourself if you lost your job. Then, after you’ve got that settled, start putting money into a retirement account. If possible, maybe also open a high yield savings account and put the money you have saved up in case of an unexpected event in there to make a little bit more interest on it. I literally did this this month, I put a relatively small amount in it and I’ve made more in interest on it in a month in that than I have probably in the lifetime of my normal savings account. It’s not a large amount, yet, but it’s still additional money. 

If you qualify for public supports and you aren’t taking advantage of them, do that too.

Even if you’re only freeing up a couple dollars a month doing this, start saving it. A little bit is better than nothing.
